record.paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
record.original_question: For wait-free linearizable register implementations of atomic snapshot objects, what are the full tradeoffs among the number of registers used, the worst-case time complexity of SCAN operations, and the worst-case time complexity of UPDATE operations?

evidence.quote: The identification of tradeoffs between the number of registers used in an implementation, the time complexity of SCAN, and the time complexity of UPDATE is another interesting open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the shared-memory model of asynchronous distributed computing with $n$ processes communicating through atomic read/write registers. An *atomic snapshot object* with $m$ components supports two operations: $\mathrm{UPDATE}(i,v)$, which writes value $v$ to component $i$, and $\mathrm{SCAN}$, which returns a vector of the current values of all $m$ components. An implementation is *linearizable* if every concurrent execution is equivalent to one in which each operation appears to take effect instantaneously at some point between its invocation and response, and *wait-free* if every process that begins an operation completes it in a finite number of its own steps, regardless of the behavior of the other processes.

For wait-free linearizable implementations of an atomic snapshot object from atomic read/write registers, determine the complete set of achievable tradeoffs among the three quantities
\[
(R,\ T_{\mathrm{SCAN}},\ T_{\mathrm{UPDATE}}),
\]
where $R$ is the number of registers used by the implementation, $T_{\mathrm{SCAN}}$ is the worst-case step complexity of a $\mathrm{SCAN}$ operation, and $T_{\mathrm{UPDATE}}$ is the worst-case step complexity of an $\mathrm{UPDATE}$ operation. Specifically, characterize, as a function of $n$ and $m$, the set of triples $(R, T_{\mathrm{SCAN}}, T_{\mathrm{UPDATE}})$ that are simultaneously realizable, with matching upper and lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: space-optimal single-scanner implementations have a tight Ω(m²) SCAN bound, and space-optimal multi-writer snapshots admit a tight Θ(mn) bound; implementations using unbounded registers achieve O(1) UPDATE and O(m) SCAN. However, a complete characterization of the three-way tradeoff among register count, SCAN time, and UPDATE time has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Lower and upper bounds for single-scanner snapshot implementations
status_evidence.snippet: In space-optimal single-scanner snapshot implementations, scans execute Ω(m²) steps.
status_evidence.claim: Tight bounds exist for the space-optimal single-scanner case but not the full three-way tradeoff.

status_evidence.title: A tight time lower bound for space-optimal implementations of multi-writer snapshots
status_evidence.snippet: For any space-optimal implementation, Ω(mn) steps are required to perform a scan.
status_evidence.claim: Space/time tradeoff is tight only at the space-optimal extreme.

status_evidence.title: Time-optimal, space-efficient single-scanner snapshots
status_evidence.snippet: T-Opt has O(1) UPDATE and O(m) SCAN but uses unbounded registers.
status_evidence.claim: Time-optimal algorithms exist but at the cost of unbounded register usage; the general tradeoff remains uncharacterized.
